content.text: No liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination charge is imposed on us anywhere in the document. I'll submit a compliant finding at the preferred level (no redline).

input.quote: After thirty consecutive days, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form without penalty and receive a refund of prepaid Fees for the unavailable period.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum charge on termination payable by us, so it sits at the preferred position rather than the fallback. Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "early termination fee", "cancellation charge", "accelerate", and every termination and payment clause (§§ 6.2, 7.1–7.5, 8.1–8.3, 9.1–9.5, 10.1–10.2, 19.4, 22.2, 24.4, 27.3) return no Customer-payable liquidated amount. § 27.3 expressly permits termination "without penalty"; § 7.1 bars any platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge the Order Form does not identify; § 7.3 bars interest on amounts ultimately found not due; § 10.2 gives us refunds rather than exit charges. The only Customer payments are Fees, transaction taxes, pre-approved expenses at cost, and, under § 22.2, audit costs plus the undisputed shortfall on a >5% underpayment — that is recovery of amounts actually owed, not a liquidated or penal sum. § 2.1's USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay volume commitment is a minimum-commitment/exit-rights issue reviewed under the minimum-commitment rule; it is not framed as liquidated damages or an early-termination fee, so we do not flag the same economics twice here. Nothing to redline; service-credit references (§§ 1.5, 7.2) run in our favour.
